open_faults.fault: mixed-universe bots mark and rank their CRYPTO holdings at the previous UTC day's close on any US weekday before the equity feed lands
open_faults.status: OPEN and ARMED - fired today, measured for the first time
open_faults.detail: Root cause unchanged: hunter_tracker.fetch() calls market_hours.trim_incomplete_bars() on a frame holding equities beside crypto, and on a weekday whose equity columns are still all-NaN the trim drops the trailing row and takes the live crypto column with it. On 08-30 this was dormant because weekend rows are kept. Today it fired. Proof is a same-cycle comparison rather than an argument: in the 13:21Z cycle crypto_state.json wrote {date 2026-08-31, implied SOL 102.78} while hunter_state.json wrote {date 2026-08-30, implied SOL 100.72}. Both bots hold SOL. Hunter understated itself by 2.2% and would have ranked any rotation on a day-old price. A skip_new_entries judgment is filed against it while it is armed. Owner decides; supervisor does not touch code.

open_faults.status: OPEN, escalated from the price-feed note

open_faults.fault: fleet loop covers only ~82% of wall-clock by design
open_faults.status: OPEN, structural, currently in a hole
open_faults.detail: bot.yml deliberately runs a 345-minute loop because GitHub accepts only about 6% of its 72 requested starts per day. Coverage is therefore ~82% and the remaining holes are unavoidable for a single job. Today's hole is the expensive kind: the 06:57Z run ended at 13:22Z, eight minutes before the US open, so no equity book marked 08-31 and no bot could act on the open. The workflow's own comments name the fix (an external trigger); this is the owner's escalation call, recorded here because the cost is now visible rather than theoretical.
